benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 2. Generate and develop original artistic ideas.
benchmarks.text: Develop ideas for media artworks using play and experimentation. For example: Combine lines and shapes in digital formats; try different drawing tools in sketching app.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 2. Generate and develop original artistic ideas.
benchmarks.text:
Plan and prototype a media artwork idea.
For example: Group brainstorm; draw a picture of idea; practice using the camera.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 2. Generate and develop original artistic ideas.
benchmarks.text:
Generate multiple ideas for media artworks through the development of sketches, models or stories.
For example: Develop soft skills through small group pitching.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 2. Generate and develop original artistic ideas.
benchmarks.text:
Generate multiple ideas for a sequenced media artwork using a variety of tools and materials.
For example: Take a series of photographs; observational drawing; journaling.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 2. Generate and develop original artistic ideas.
benchmarks.text:
Generate multiple ideas for media artworks using a variety of creative methods that explore time and motion.
For example: Investigation with video; reverse designing media artswork; mindmapping.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 2. Generate and develop original artistic ideas.
benchmarks.text:
Develop and test ideas, plans, models, and proposals for media artworks, considering artistic goals and audience.
For example: Draw a layout of a stop motion set; practice in and compare different sound recording spaces; interview or investigate audience for a project.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 2. Generate and develop original artistic ideas.
benchmarks.text:
Organize and propose artistic ideas, plans, prototypes, and processes for media artworks, considering expressive intent.
For example: Sketching; modeling; sequencing.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 2. Generate and develop original artistic ideas.
benchmarks.text:
Design, propose and evaluate artistic ideas, plans, prototypes, and production processes for media artworks, considering expressive intent and resources.
For example: Pitching; storyboarding.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 2. Generate and develop original artistic ideas.
benchmarks.text:
Structure and critique ideas and solutions for original media artworks, using divergent thinking and identified generative methods.
For example: Compare and contrast App-based animation platforms; repeatedly abstract an object for a 2D design.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 2. Generate and develop original artistic ideas.
benchmarks.text:
Apply aesthetic criteria in developing, proposing, and refining artistic ideas, plans, prototypes, and production processes for media artworks, considering original inspirations, audience and constraints.
For example: Survey; research; design thinking; identify problem.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 3. Create original artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Capture ideas in media artworks.
For example: Take pictures considering space; use recording materials; assemble different lines and shapes in design app.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 3. Create original artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Choose and use a media arts tool to capture an idea.
For example: Camera; digital drawing; sound recording.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 3. Create original artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Choose and use sketches, models or stories to create unified media artworks.
For example: Use storyboard to make a stop motion; Pick from thumbnail sketches for graphic design.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 3. Create original artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Construct media arts content to communicate a purpose or idea, using elements of artistic foundations.
For example: Photo collage considering attention; poster design considering composition; character design and development considering convention.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 3. Create original artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Structure and arrange content and components to convey purpose and meaning in the creation of media artworks, applying artistic foundations.
For example: Hand drawn animation considering balance and contrast; design music for video clip considering emphasis; photo manipulation considering fairness, fair use, juxaposition, and imaging.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 3. Create original artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Create content and combine components for a specific audience to express purpose and meaning in media artworks, utilizing artistic foundations.
For example: Stop motion animation considering force and exaggeration; live action filmaking considering narrative structure; digital self-portraits exploring identity and meaning.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 3. Create original artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Experiment with multiple approaches to produce content and components for a specific purpose in media artworks, utilizing a range of artistic foundations.
For example: Digital illustration considering perspective; clay animation considering point of view; poster design considering media messages.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 3. Create original artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Create media artworks, using artistic foundations, that integrate production processes, content, and stylistic conventions to communicate meaning for a specific audience.
For example: Choose and defend a narrative structure for video.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 3. Create original artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Create media artworks using transdisciplinary or transmedia production, to express emotion and meaning.
For example: Original sound design (such as an experiential design incorporating a podcast) considering theme, movement and unity; simple web page design condsidering positioning with multimodal perception.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 3. Create original artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Create media artworks using hybridization or multimodal perception, by integrating components and stylistic conventions, to express compelling purpose, story, or emotion.
For example: Set building with light, motion or interactivity; character development, type selection considering multiple presentation formats.

2. Create media arts productions in a variety of genres, considering critical media literacies, aesthetic criteria, communication goals, and audience using artistic foundations.
For example: Magazine layout considering space and sequence specifically through typography, messaging, and audience; game world design considering narrative structure.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 4. Revise and complete original artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Make changes to the content of media artworks and share results.
For example: Rearrange objects in a digital drawing; rerecord video.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 4. Revise and complete original artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
After reviewing media artwork, make changes to the form of the work.
For example: The order of sequencing photos; the color of objects and images.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 4. Revise and complete original artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Test and describe expressive effects in altering, revising, and completing media artworks.
For example: Changing the frame rate in an animation; comparing spacing in a design; trying different shot types for an action.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 4. Revise and complete original artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
When revising media artworks compare and contrast how the emphasis of elements alters effect and purpose.
For example: Use of space in live action filming; manipulation of light in an image.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 4. Revise and complete original artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Revise content to convey purpose and meaning in various media artworks, using artistic foundations.
For example: Editing filters considering texture, editing, and mixing qualities considering sound elements.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 4. Revise and complete original artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Based on feedback, revise media artworks to improve clarity and purpose.
For example: Review balance of components, including juxtaposition.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 4. Revise and complete original artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Evaluate how elements and components can be altered for intentional effects and audience.
For example: Font and image size and placement; sound selection and rearragement in video considering stylistic convention.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 4. Revise and complete original artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Improve media artworks by placing emphasis on particular expressive components.
For example: Consideration of continuity, purpose, audience, or place.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 4. Revise and complete original artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Refine media artworks, resisting closure while intentionally altering stylistic conventions based on specific goals and personal choices.
For example: Edit video game level design considering interactive components after receiving feedback.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 4. Revise and complete original artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Modify media artworks by improving technical quality, components, and stylistic conventions, based on consideration of purpose, audience, and place.
For example: Redesign webpage based on a specific project goal.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 5. Develop and refine artistic techniques and work for performance.
benchmarks.text:
Identify different ways media artworks are presented.
For example: Look at, listen to, or experience media arts presentations.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 5. Develop and refine artistic techniques and work for performance.
benchmarks.text:
Sort media artwork by styles and types.
For example: Comparing work by a single artist.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 5. Develop and refine artistic techniques and work for performance.
benchmarks.text:
Identify techniques and sequencing in media artworks.

For example: Flipbooks; storyboard; frames for stop motion.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 5. Develop and refine artistic techniques and work for performance.
benchmarks.text:
Discuss techniques used in editing media artworks.
For example: Cutting and splicing; volume; transitions; fade.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 5. Develop and refine artistic techniques and work for performance.
benchmarks.text:
Combine and coordinate a variety of media content into a media artwork presentation.
For example: A mixed media performance.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 5. Develop and refine artistic techniques and work for performance.
benchmarks.text:
Organize multiple media artworks to be combined into a single presentation.

For example: A media broadcast.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 5. Develop and refine artistic techniques and work for performance.
benchmarks.text:
Evaluate how the public uses, relates to, and participates with media artworks.
For example: Social media platforms; public space artworks.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 5. Develop and refine artistic techniques and work for performance.
benchmarks.text:
Explain the choices made in the presentation of media artworks.
For example: Choices made in creative components such as sound, titling, etc.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 5. Develop and refine artistic techniques and work for performance.
benchmarks.text:
Develop and apply criteria for evaluating a collection of media artwork for presentation.
For example: Create survey for a focus group; participate in forum on media artwork presentation.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 5. Develop and refine artistic techniques and work for performance.
benchmarks.text:
Critique and justify the use of design components within a media arts presentation, considering the reaction of the audience.
For example: Director Q&A; stakeholder review; SCAMPER; six thinking hats.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 6. Make artistic choices in order to convey meaning through performance.
benchmarks.text:
Explain the message of a media artwork.
For example: Compare cereal box design for intended audience.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 6. Make artistic choices in order to convey meaning through performance.
benchmarks.text:
Identify where you see media arts in the community.
For example: Bank kiosk, billboards.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 6. Make artistic choices in order to convey meaning through performance.
benchmarks.text:
Compare and contrast venues where media arts are shared and their effects on the audience.

For example: Explore media environments like movie theatre, computer, home movie.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 6. Make artistic choices in order to convey meaning through performance.
benchmarks.text:
Explain how the meaning of a media artwork might change depending on the venue.
For example: Formal vs informal (movie theater vs at home); still photo vs. film.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 6. Make artistic choices in order to convey meaning through performance.
benchmarks.text:
Identfy and describe presentation conditions, and take on a role in presenting media artworks.
For example: Exporting and distributing completed movie into online portfolio.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 6. Make artistic choices in order to convey meaning through performance.
benchmarks.text:
Explain different roles related to presenting media artworks, and fullfill one of those roles in a presentation.
For example: Director; writer; actor; presenter.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 6. Make artistic choices in order to convey meaning through performance.
benchmarks.text:
Analyze various presentation formats and fulfill various tasks and defined processes in the presentation or distribution of media artworks.
For example: Virtual channels; formatting and exporting for various print production.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 6. Make artistic choices in order to convey meaning through performance.
benchmarks.text:
Evaluate how various presentation formats and approaches to distribution can have a personal or local impact.
For example: Compare and contrast presentation for a museum with commercial signage.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 6. Make artistic choices in order to convey meaning through performance.
benchmarks.text:
Evaluate and implement improvements in the presention of media artworks, considering personal and local impacts.
For example: Research the changes to personal or corporate branding over time.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 6. Make artistic choices in order to convey meaning through performance.
benchmarks.text:
Design and evaluate presentation and distribution of media artworks through multiple formats for specific contexts, market(s) and system(s).
For example: Evaluate presentation modes for media artworks through virtual channels versus a multimedia theatre, considering media arts contexts.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 7. Analyze and construct interpretations of artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Identify components (such as sound, lighting, sequence, mood) in media artworks.
For example: List parts of a movie such as beginning, middle, and end.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 7. Analyze and construct interpretations of artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Identify components and messages in media artworks.
For example: List parts of a movie such as beginning, middle and end, and identify how these parts tell stories or share messages.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 7. Analyze and construct interpretations of artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Identify and describe the components and messages in media artworks, and share how the work creates different experiences.

For example: Watch a suspenseful video and discuss feelings and why.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 7. Analyze and construct interpretations of artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Identify and describe how messages are created by components in media artworks, and share how the components affect mood.
For example: Watch a variety of media arts clips and discuss different clips express or influence different moods.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 7. Analyze and construct interpretations of artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Compare how messages are created by components in media artworks, and explain how the components affect mood and audience experience.
For example: Watch a variety of media arts clips and discuss how different clips express mood, and how they affect how the audience experiences the media art works.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 7. Analyze and construct interpretations of artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Differentiate how components in media artworks impact message and mood to create meaning and how they affect audience experience.
For example: Analyze how lighting design and sound design in a film impact mood and audience experience.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 7. Analyze and construct interpretations of artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Analyze how messages change due to multiple approaches in producing media artworks and how they affect audience experience.
For example: Examine media artworks that use different technological approaches, such as interactivity versus theatrical film, and the affect on audience experience.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 7. Analyze and construct interpretations of artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Analyze how intentional use of elements of media artworks interact with personal perceptions, influencing mood and managing audience experience.
For example: Examine how media artworks include a variety of media elements which affect the way we see, hear, or experience a media artwork.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 7. Analyze and construct interpretations of artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Analyze the relationships between media arts components, and explain how transdisciplinary or transmedia productions communicate and affect audience experience.
For example: Compare the experience of platforms with interactivity (such as experiential design) with the experience of traditional art mediums.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 7. Analyze and construct interpretations of artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Analyze how a broad range of media artworks affect experience and communicate through multimodal perception, while using artistic foundations.
For example: Analyze the managed experience in augmented reality, virtual worlds or gaming that incorporates artificial intelligence.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 8. Evaluate artistic work by applying criteria.
benchmarks.text:
Share reactions to media artworks.
For example: Stating personal selection of a sound or image experience.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 8. Evaluate artistic work by applying criteria.
benchmarks.text:
Identify effective parts and possible changes to media artworks.
For example: Utilize a process to provide and use feedback such as praise/polish/ponder activities.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 8. Evaluate artistic work by applying criteria.
benchmarks.text:
Discuss the effectiveness of and improvements for media artworks, considering their context.
For example: Change the color, texture or feel of a digital illustration to improve the tone of the media artwork.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 8. Evaluate artistic work by applying criteria.
benchmarks.text:
Evaluate media artworks and identify possible improvements based on given criteria.
For example: Discuss how given criteria are evident in a media artwork and suggest ways to improve the media artwork such as keeping movements smaller and more controlled in stopmotion animation, or use of techniques to stabilize the captured video, or how to increase focus in digital images.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 8. Evaluate artistic work by applying criteria.
benchmarks.text:
Apply given criteria for evaluating and improving media artworks and production processes.
For example: Keeping movements smaller and more controlled in stopmotion animation, use of techniques to stabilize the captured video, or how to increase focus in digital images.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 8. Evaluate artistic work by applying criteria.
benchmarks.text:
Develop and apply criteria to evaluate media artworks and production processes.
For example: As a group, collaboratively develop a list of criteria to be used in evaluating a media artwork including how the media artwork was produced/created.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 8. Evaluate artistic work by applying criteria.
benchmarks.text:
Provide and receive constructive feedback based on criteria for evaluating media artworks.
For example: Create a rubric for a project.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 8. Evaluate artistic work by applying criteria.
benchmarks.text:
Compare and contrast an evaluation of a media artwork based on personal criteria and an evaluation of a media artwork based on a set of established criteria.
For example: Complete a self assessment and compare it with assesment from peer or educator.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 8. Evaluate artistic work by applying criteria.
benchmarks.text:
Evaluate media artworks and production processes with developed criteria at multiple stages in the creation process, including criteria related to fair use and copyright.**
For example: Plagiarism; appropriation; intellectual property; creative commons media; public domain; and legal.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 8. Evaluate artistic work by applying criteria.
benchmarks.text:
Construct and defend evaluations of media artworks and production processes, including criteria related to ethics. **
For example: Respond to representations of people, identity or groups in media artworks.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 9. Integrate knowledge and personal experiences while responding to, creating, and presenting artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Use personal experiences in creating media artworks.
For example: Personal stories; media art works that display personal life experience.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 9. Integrate knowledge and personal experiences while responding to, creating, and presenting artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Use personal experiences and interests in creating media artworks.
For example: Personal stories; media art works that display personal life experience; or media artworks that exhibit choices of content/tools.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 9. Integrate knowledge and personal experiences while responding to, creating, and presenting artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Use personal experiences, interests, and research in creating media artworks.
For example: Personal stories; media art works that display personal life experience; or media artworks that exhibit research to create story.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 9. Integrate knowledge and personal experiences while responding to, creating, and presenting artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Identify and show how media artworks form meaning, situations, and culture.
For example: Popular media.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 9. Integrate knowledge and personal experiences while responding to, creating, and presenting artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Examine and use personal interests, research, and cultural understanding to create media artworks.
For example: Autobiographical stories; creating media artworks illustrating personal statements/positions; media art works that display personal life experiences.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 9. Integrate knowledge and personal experiences while responding to, creating, and presenting artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Access and use multiple resources related to cultural understanding to create media artworks.
For example: Interests, knowledge, and experiences.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 9. Integrate knowledge and personal experiences while responding to, creating, and presenting artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
1.Compare and constrast how creating and presenting media artworks forms personal and digital identity.**
For example: Using platforms of systematic communications, distribution and engagement with new media.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 9. Integrate knowledge and personal experiences while responding to, creating, and presenting artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Analyze how to safely, ethically and intentionally develop digital identity when creating and presenting media artworks, through systematic communications.**
For example: Ethically exploring anonymity in a virtual world such as gaming; digital safety; digital security.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 9. Integrate knowledge and personal experiences while responding to, creating, and presenting artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Evaluate the cycle of producing media artworks to make meaning of and respond to local and global events, and the power of media arts to affect social change.
For example: Artmaking in response to natural disaster; political and social campaigns.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 9. Integrate knowledge and personal experiences while responding to, creating, and presenting artistic work.
benchmarks.text:
Incorporate personal experiences and cultural perspectives to establish personal aesthetic in media artworks.

2. Analyze how individually developed media messages influence local and global communities.
For example: Disruption of the dominant discourse through media artworks; responsibly and irresponsibly developed media messages.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 10. Demonstrate an understanding that artistic works influence and are influenced by personal, societal, cultural, and historical contexts, including the contributions of Minnesota American Indian tribes and communities.
benchmarks.text:
Identify how media arts are a part of life.
For example: Name places media arts are found in our daily life and how they are used, such as smartphones.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 10. Demonstrate an understanding that artistic works influence and are influenced by personal, societal, cultural, and historical contexts, including the contributions of Minnesota American Indian tribes and communities.
benchmarks.text: Describe media art from various times and places. For example: Describe how media arts has changed over time, such as hand drawn cel animation to computer generated animations; describe how media arts has existed in theaters and television, but now also exist online, within apps, social media, personal devices, smartphones, etc; describe how media arts exists across the world.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 10. Demonstrate an understanding that artistic works influence and are influenced by personal, societal, cultural, and historical contexts, including the contributions of Minnesota American Indian tribes and communities.
benchmarks.text:
Discuss how media artworks relate to everyday cultural life.

For example: Describe how media arts is used in our everyday life, how it influences what we think, and how it can be used in our lives.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 10. Demonstrate an understanding that artistic works influence and are influenced by personal, societal, cultural, and historical contexts, including the contributions of Minnesota American Indian tribes and communities.
benchmarks.text:
Explain how knowing the time and place in which a media artwork was made influences interpretation of the work.
For example: Describe how labor-intensive films and animations used to be when they were shot frame-by-frame or by creating using cel animation techniques; describe how special effects in film have changed over time and how they impact what media artists are able to communicate.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 10. Demonstrate an understanding that artistic works influence and are influenced by personal, societal, cultural, and historical contexts, including the contributions of Minnesota American Indian tribes and communities.
benchmarks.text:
Identify how media artworks are used to inform or change beliefs, values or behaviors of an individual or society.
For example: Identify how media arts influences what we perceive, think, or believe; identify how media arts can influence our culture for positive change.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 10. Demonstrate an understanding that artistic works influence and are influenced by personal, societal, cultural, and historical contexts, including the contributions of Minnesota American Indian tribes and communities.
benchmarks.text:
Make inferences about the time, place, or culture in which a media artwork was created, citing evidence.
For example: Evaluate different video game designs for their history and context.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 10. Demonstrate an understanding that artistic works influence and are influenced by personal, societal, cultural, and historical contexts, including the contributions of Minnesota American Indian tribes and communities.
benchmarks.text:
Explain how media artworks relate to and impact personal, societal, cultural, historical, and community situations.
For example: Personal identity; digital identity; historical events; entertainment.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 10. Demonstrate an understanding that artistic works influence and are influenced by personal, societal, cultural, and historical contexts, including the contributions of Minnesota American Indian tribes and communities.
benchmarks.text:
Analyze how response to media art is influenced by understanding the time and place in which it was created, the available resources, and cultural uses.
For example: Evaluate the changes in the use and style of photography over time.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 10. Demonstrate an understanding that artistic works influence and are influenced by personal, societal, cultural, and historical contexts, including the contributions of Minnesota American Indian tribes and communities.
benchmarks.text:
Explain different ways media arts are used to represent, establish, reinforce, and reflect culture or group identity.
For example: Use of memes and viral video in systematic communications.

benchmarks.subject: art
benchmarks.standard: 10. Demonstrate an understanding that artistic works influence and are influenced by personal, societal, cultural, and historical contexts, including the contributions of Minnesota American Indian tribes and communities.
benchmarks.text:
Synthesize how media arts represent, establish, reinforce, and reflect culture or group identity.

2. Use contexts, purposes, representations, and values to inform media artworks.
For example: Develop media literacy to examine how media messages affect social trends, power, equity, bias, gender, personal or cultural identity.
